 Firemen rescue 16 elderly residents from Kluang flash flood
 Amirull Salihing 45 seconds ago Add comment 3 min read 
 Learn how Kluang firemen rescued 16 elderly residents aged 65 to 85 after flash floods hit a Jalan Haji Manan nursing home on 17 November.
 Photo: Wong Shu Qi FB 
 Firemen rescued 16 elderly residents from a nursing home hit by flash floods following a heavy downpour in Kluang on 17 November 2026. Rising floodwaters surrounded the facility along Jalan Haji Manan, prompting an urgent late-afternoon evacuation before water levels could enter the building.
 According to Malay Mail , the Kluang Fire and Rescue Station received an emergency distress call at 5:11 pm. Twelve firemen immediately mobilised to the scene, located roughly one kilometre from the fire station.
 For Kluang families and caregivers, the swift rescue underscores how quickly northeast monsoon downpours can inundate low-lying urban streets. Rapid coordination ensured vulnerable seniors reached dry shelter safely without injuries.

 Swift 20-minute evacuation along Jalan Haji Manan
 Photo: Wong Shu Qi FB 
 In a press statement, Kluang Fire and Rescue Station operations commander Fadly A. Karim detailed how the response team deployed. Firemen arrived with one Fire Rescue Tender vehicle and a four-wheel-drive unit to navigate rising street runoff.
 Upon reaching Jalan Haji Manan, personnel discovered flash floodwaters surrounding the nursing home had exceeded 0.6 metres, or about two feet. Deep water blocked standard exits and posed an immediate hazard to mobility-impaired residents inside.
 Working quickly in the rain, firemen carried and escorted 16 elderly residents out of the inundated compound to higher ground. The evacuated group comprised 14 men and two women aged between 65 and 85 years old.

 Temporary relocation to Yap Tau Sah homestay
 Photo: Wong Shu Qi FB 
 Following the initial evacuation, emergency responders arranged safe overnight accommodation away from the flood-prone Jalan Haji Manan stretch. All 16 seniors were relocated to a homestay in Jalan 17, Yap Tau Sah, where care routines could continue uninterrupted.
 Moving elderly care home residents requires careful coordination to protect medication schedules, mobility aids, and personal comfort during sudden weather emergencies. Temporary homestay placement kept the entire group together under staff supervision while floodwaters receded.
 Low-lying pockets around central Kluang, including Jalan Haji Manan, remain susceptible to rapid surface runoff during intense afternoon thunderstorms. Blocked drains and overflowing roadside culverts can cause water levels to spike within minutes during heavy rainfall.
 Local care centres and families with elderly relatives benefit from keeping emergency contact numbers and waterproof medication kits packed during monsoon months.
 Monsoon preparedness for Johor families and care homes
 Photo: Wong Shu Qi FB 
 With Malaysia in the northeast monsoon season, the Malaysian Meteorological Department regularly issues afternoon thunderstorm warnings across Johor’s interior districts. Care operators in flood-prone zones are advised to monitor drainage levels whenever sustained rain falls after 3:00 pm.
 See also   Kampung Melayu Subang floods hit 92 homes as river rises Residents facing rising floodwaters or needing urgent evacuation assistance should immediately dial the national emergency hotline at 999. Providing clear landmarks and noting whether elderly or bedridden occupants are inside helps fire crews deploy four-wheel-drive support faster.
 Community members can also check real-time river and rainfall alerts through the Department of Irrigation and Drainage Public Info Banjir portal. Early warnings give families and care centres crucial extra minutes to move vehicles, medical supplies, and vulnerable relatives to safety.
 Thanks to the 20-minute response by Kluang firemen, all 16 seniors weathered the flash flood safely.
